A1.justification: Both complete 16-page PDFs describe SwiftTS. Their text, equations, figures, tables, algorithm, and Appendices A.1–A.5 are readable and can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original SwiftTS model-selection evaluations, ablations, and runtime comparisons in Section 5, plus sensitivity and attention analyses in Appendix A.5.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results in Section 5 and Appendix A.5, including model-selection comparisons, ablations, sensitivity studies, and attention visualizations.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same dual encoders, patchwise cross-attention, joint loss, horizon-adaptive experts, and cross-task meta-learning procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 14 forecasting datasets across six domains and retain the same cross-dataset, cross-horizon, and IID/OOD scenarios. Section 5 and Appendix A.1 show no coverage changes.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain RankME, LogME, Regression, Etran, DISCO, Model Spider, and zero-shot comparisons. The comparator membership in the Figure 4 runtime analyses is also unchanged.

E3.justification: The eight candidate models, four forecasting horizons, dataset splits, three-dataset holdout protocol, evaluation metrics, and 80-epoch training budget remain unchanged. No experimental protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: Table 3, Figure 4, and Appendix A.5 retain identical embedding and cross-task ablations, IID/OOD comparisons, efficiency analyses, loss-coefficient and expert-count sensitivity studies, and attention visualizations.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same point estimates and averages. Neither supplies repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged, including the appendix results. For example, Table 2 reports SwiftTS's average weighted Kendall correlation as 0.442 and Pr(top1) as 0.339 in both versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and Equations (1)–(11), including Appendix A.3, are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same novelty, method-contribution, state-of-the-art performance, efficiency, and generalization claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of the embeddings, cross-task learning, scalability, sensitivity studies, and attention patterns remain identical. No applicability qualification, failure condition, or limitation is added or revised.

D1.justification: The page 10 Reproducibility Statement replaces the anonymous 4open.science code/data address with the decisionintelligence/SwiftTS repository address on GitHub. Both versions already claim a release; implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, and pseudocode remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, the bibliography, and the positioning relative to feature-analytic and learning-based selection methods are unchanged. The conference-publication header does not revise the relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: v2 adds the text 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026' and rearranges the author email lines. The scientific prose, terminology, section order, and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds a running publication header and slightly adjusts first-page spacing through the more compact email block. All six figures, four tables, and the algorithm retain their content, formatting, captions, and placement.

improvement.justification: The scientific exposition, methods, experimental evidence, and appendix analyses are unchanged. v2 updates publication formatting and an existing code/data address; both versions already provide access information. These administrative edits do not establish a meaningful overall quality improvement or deterioration.
